posts.text: Our troops risk their lives to defend our nation. Toxic burn pit exposure should never leave them fighting another battle long after they return home.  That is why I helped introduce the bipartisan WIPE OUT Burn Pits Act to identify and track dangerous burn pits near U.S. forces,

Children battling rare diseases cannot afford to wait. A rare diagnosis should never mean a child is left behind in the search for lifesaving treatments.  My bipartisan Priority for Pediatric Cures Actwould permanently authorize the FDA’s Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher Program, giving researchers and innovators the long-term certainty needed to invest in treatments for children with few or no options.  Developing a treatment can take years, but investment decisions are being made today. Families deserve hope, and promising research deserves the opportunity to move forward.  I urge my colleagues to expedite passage of this critical legislation. Every child deserves a chance at a healthier future. Let’s get this done!

It was a pleasure to meet with Cory Price, the new Director of James A. Haley Veterans’ Hospital, and his leadership team to discuss concerns local Veterans have shared with me. Their experiences guide my work to improve access to timely, high-quality care and ensure their concerns receive the attention they deserve.  I was encouraged by updates on construction at the new Lecanto and Brooksville clinics, as well as the new Community Living Center in Lutz. These projects represent important investments in care for Veterans throughout our region.  I also appreciated Director Price’s commitment to improving the VA’s regional phone system, which has been a persistent source of frustration for many Veterans, and his willingness to address concerns about declining referrals to the Veteran Directed Care program.  I look forward to building a strong working relationship with Director Price and his team, maintaining open communication, and working together to address the challenges facing Veterans and their families. Those who served our nation deserve a VA that listens, responds, and delivers.

On October 28, we commemorate Oxi Day and honor the courage of the Greek people, who stood against fascism in 1940 with a resounding “OXI”—“NO!” Their refusal to surrender their freedom remains an enduring example of bravery, unity, and sacrifice.  As a proud Greek American, I carry deep gratitude for those who defended Greece and preserved the heritage we cherish. Their example reminds us that freedom requires courage and that standing up to tyranny matters, even against overwhelming odds.  May we honor their legacy by defending liberty and passing their remarkable story on to future generations.

Veterans battling a devastating disease shouldn’t also have to battle bureaucracy for the benefits they’ve earned.  I’m proud to lead a bipartisan, bicameral letter, joined by 53 lawmakers, urging the VA to recognize Inclusion Body Myositis (IBM) as a presumptive service-connected condition. This would help Veterans living with this rare, progressive, incurable muscle disease access disability benefits without individually proving their illness is linked to military service.  Our Veterans deserve answers, fair treatment, and timely support. I’ll keep fighting for them.

Expanding training opportunities and building pathways into maritime careers will help ensure we have the welders, engineers, shipbuilders, and other skilled professionals needed to keep America competitive. I remain committed to supporting American workers and strengthening our nation’s maritime capabilities.
